title: Post-quantum secure messaging over a replicated log
description: A group-messaging service whose epoch keys reach members in hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 welcomes, whose sealed messages are committed on a 3-node Raft log with seeded leader crashes, and whose API uses Idempotency-Keys, a transactional outbox and a versioned envelope contract. The project is about the four seams where these meet, and it breaks each one on purpose.
outcome: You can build an encrypted, replicated, retry-safe message service and prove its integration contracts. Nonces stay unique across failovers, rotation survives log replay, retries never show twice, and envelope versions switch on every replica at once. Each property has a seeded fault and a fitness function.
environment: Python 3.12 (validated on Linux), cryptography 50.0.2 (ML-KEM-768, X25519, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF, AES-GCM-SIV for tryIt 1), stdlib sqlite3. Reuses cryptography L400 #17/#18/#20, L300 #15, L500 #24; distributed-systems L300 #12, L100 #5; application-architecture L200 #9, L300 #14 (imported in place through _kb.py). No network, no containers.
overview: Three tested building blocks (a hybrid PQ key exchange with AES-GCM, a Raft log, and retry-safe APIs with versioned contracts) become one messaging service. The bugs that matter appear only where they meet: a nonce counter that a new leader restarts, an epoch key a replay cannot find, a retry that becomes a second ciphertext, and a format version one replica accepts early. Each seam has a test that fails under its seeded fault.

glossary.meaning: One group key period. A log entry starts it with hybrid welcomes; every envelope names its epoch.
ML-KEM-768 + X25519 encapsulation to a member's key package plus the AES-GCM-wrapped epoch secret: 1,180 B.
The service identity on the Raft leader that encrypts messages; it learns epoch keys from its own welcome in the log.
A boundary where two topics' assumptions meet; here each has a contract, a risk and a test that fails under a seeded fault.

concepts: Nonce uniqueness is a distributed property: no state (random) or state consensus already makes unique (term || counter).
Rotation must be replayable: keys travel in the log, envelopes name their epoch, log order defines membership.
Idempotency belongs in replicated state; with randomized encryption duplicates are different bytes.
Format versions are switched by the log, not by node config.

designBrief.context: A team chat for a small company stores every message for years on a 3-replica log that survives node crashes. Clients retry on any timeout. Members join and leave. Recorded traffic must stay confidential against a future quantum attacker, and the envelope format will change.
constraints: 0 reused (epoch key, nonce) pairs across 10,000 messages with seeded leader crashes (about 1% per request)
all 3 replicas show identical plaintext lists = exactly the acknowledged messages (0 lost, 0 duplicates)
no plaintext in any replica's log or any node's outbox; replicas hold no keys
per-member key package + welcome <= 2,400 B (lesson 18's key-share budget); welcome <= 1,200 B
a removed member reads 0 messages ordered after her removal; a fresh device replays history from index 1
retries: 400 without a key, 200 replay, 422 on a changed payload; one message shown per key even after failover
a new envelope version is enabled on every replica at the same log index; unknown versions refused, no fallback
at most 2^32 messages per epoch key (NIST SP 800-38D random-IV limit)
designBrief.question: How do the crypto, replication and API patterns have to change so that their combination keeps these properties, and how do we prove each seam?

architecture.summary: Clients POST with an Idempotency-Key to the API on the Raft leader (pqmsg.Service.post). The API checks replicated state for the key. The sealer, a service identity welcomed into each epoch, encrypts under the current epoch key with a random 96-bit nonce, inside a v2 envelope whose header is the AAD. The sealed envelope goes into the node's SQLite outbox (lesson 9's schema), and lesson 9's Relay proposes it to lesson 12's Raft cluster until it commits. replicated_state.State.apply runs on every replica: it dedupes by key and keyed fingerprint, rejects stale epochs and non-members, and enforces the replicated version gate. Rotations and the gate are log entries too. Member devices and a new leader's sealer replay the log from index 1 to learn epoch keys from their hybrid welcomes.

seams.contract: every (epoch key, 96-bit nonce) pair is used once, whoever is leader; the sealer keeps no nonce state (or derives it from the term, which consensus makes unique)
seams.risk: a leader-local counter restarts at 1 on every new leader: 109 reused nonces after 49 failovers, and keystream XOR reveals a message

seams.contract: epoch secrets travel in the log as hybrid welcomes; envelopes name their epoch; an envelope must match the epoch current at its log index
seams.risk: replay fails after rotation (newest key used for old ciphertexts), or a late epoch-1 envelope is shown to a member removed before its log position

seams.contract: Idempotency-Key + keyed fingerprint are in every entry; dedupe happens in the replicated state machine; the outbox relays at least once
seams.risk: a retry after failover is sealed again (a new ciphertext) and the stuck outbox row is relayed later, so readers see the message twice (32 duplicates in 300 messages without apply-time dedupe)

seams.contract: envelope header {v, aead, kem, epoch, sender, ikey, n} checked against the reader contract; accepted versions are replicated state switched by a log entry
seams.risk: a renamed field breaks readers; a node-local version setting makes replicas show different messages (3 / 5 / 3)

failureLab.inject: python run_project.py --inject leader-counter: the sealer uses the shipped nonce_derived.DerivedNonce, a counter in the leader's memory that ignores the Raft term. It shows up only when AES-GCM (crypto) meets leader failover (Raft).
failureLab.symptom: seam and F1 lines FAIL. Lesson 15's offline scan finds 109 reused (epoch, nonce) pairs after 49 failovers in 1,500 messages, and XOR with one known message recovers 'msg 00010 from bob: status green'.
failureLab.diagnose: Group the reused nonces: their values are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 ... under one epoch key, and every collision pairs envelopes sealed by different leaders. The counter restarted at 1 on each new leader, and on each restart, because it is volatile and not replicated.
failureLab.fix: Default: random 96-bit nonces with a per-epoch cap of 2^32 messages (ADR-01-1). Alternative (build task): nonce = term (4 B) || per-term counter (8 B). Raft's Election Safety makes it unique while only the leader seals; this is NIST SP 800-38D's deterministic construction with the term as the fixed field.
failureLab.test: labs/L600/01-pq-replicated-messaging/tests/test_p01_failure_lab.py (fault -> reuse and recovered plaintext; default -> 0 reuse on the same failovers) and labs/L600/01-pq-replicated-messaging/tests/test_p01_build_task.py (BUILD_TARGET=mine: FAILED (failures=4); solution: OK)

buildTask.task: Fix nonce_derived.py (shipped faulty: leader-local counter) so DerivedNonce.next(term) returns 12 bytes that never repeat across leaders or restarts under one epoch key and refuses a term that goes backwards. Keep the interface; the service passes the current Raft term.
buildTask.acceptance: tests/test_p01_build_task.py: 5 tests. Disjoint nonces for leaders in terms 3 and 4; no overlap after a restart in a later term; ValueError on term 5 -> 4; 12 bytes; 400 messages with seeded failovers through the real Service give 0 reuse. Switch: BUILD_TARGET=mine tests your nonce_derived.py; the default tests the solution.

scalingLimits: Per-key volume: random nonces cap an epoch key at 2^32 messages, which is 4.97 days at 10,000 messages/s. Signal: messages-per-epoch approaching the cap, or 409 rotation_required. Rotate by volume or move to term || counter.

Group size: pairwise welcomes are O(members). 100 members make a 164,659 B epoch entry (119,180 B raw welcomes) replicated to every node. Signal: rotation latency and Raft append size spikes on membership changes. Move to a ratchet tree (MLS, RFC 9420).

History and restarts: no snapshots, so every restart replays the log from index 1. The 10k run made 1,061,514 state-machine applies (about 106 per message) across 205 restarts. Signal: recovery time growing with log length, and an unbounded dedupe table. Add snapshots and a published key-expiry window.

codeWalkthrough.title: _kb.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Loads modules from the other topics' labs by path. A cached module of the same name from another lab (helpers, solution_strict) is evicted first, so nothing clashes and nothing is copied.

codeWalkthrough.title: group_crypto.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Device = lesson 18 key package (1,216 B). welcome() = server_respond + AES-GCM-wrapped epoch secret (1,180 B). learn() uses the strict client (a 32-byte downgrade raises HandshakeError). seal() puts the whole header in the AAD and uses lesson 17's registry by id. contract_problems() checks the header against lesson 14-style like() matchers.

codeWalkthrough.title: replicated_state.State.apply
codeWalkthrough.detail: Deterministic per committed entry: epoch entries advance the epoch; contract entries set accepted versions; messages are checked in the order version -> epoch -> membership -> dedupe (duplicate / conflict). Faults switch off one rule each.

codeWalkthrough.title: pqmsg.Service.post
codeWalkthrough.detail: KEY_RE check (400), replay from replicated seen (200 or 422), version/limit gate (409), seal with the node's nonce source, outbox insert in one SQLite transaction, Relay to Raft. Chaos can crash the leader after the outbox write or after propose (503).

codeWalkthrough.title: pqmsg.Service.publish / sync / restart
codeWalkthrough.detail: publish is the bus lesson 9's Relay calls: propose, then tick until committed or raise NotCommitted. sync applies newly committed entries and lets the sealer learn epoch keys from its welcome. restart rebuilds all volatile state (state machine, sealer keys, nonce source) by replay.

codeWalkthrough.title: harness.py + scenarios.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: FastCluster skips lesson 12's per-tick full safety scan (too slow at 10k entries) and runs the SafetyChecker on demand. send() is the client: one key per message, created before the retry loop. nonce_reuse() runs lesson 15's scan per epoch. scenarios.py holds the seeded milestones, seams and fitness functions.

codeWalkthrough.title: run_project.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Prints one JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function plus the scorecard, and exits 1 on any failure. --inject applies a fault to every scenario; leader-counter also prints the failure_lab line with the keystream recovery.

inRealSystems: Messaging Layer Security (RFC 9420) binds every message to an epoch, and members process Commits in one agreed order. That is the epoch-in-the-log idea, with a ratchet tree instead of pairwise welcomes.
TLS 1.3 deployments negotiate X25519MLKEM768 (RFC 10024, IANA 0x11EC) for the same harvest-now-decrypt-later reason as the welcomes here.
Raft-based stores (etcd, Consul) dedupe client retries inside the state machine with client sessions, as the Raft paper section 8 describes and as ADR-01-2 does.
useWhen: Use this shape whenever encrypted data is written through a replicated or retried pipeline: keep nonce state out of leader memory, put keys and versions where replay can find them, and dedupe by key in replicated state. Avoid it for a single-writer, single-node store, where a plain counter nonce and a local table are enough.
simulatorVsReal: Raft is lesson 12's in-process simulation: ticks instead of time, no disk, no snapshots, crashes chosen by a seeded RNG. Real deployments add fsync, network partitions with clocks, and snapshot transfer. The sealer is a service-side identity (an encryption gateway). In a pure end-to-end app the sender's device seals, and the nonce lesson applies to multi-device senders. The welcome is a teaching construction modelled on lesson 18. Production would use HPKE with a PQ/T KEM or MLS.
caution: Learning code. Never ship a nonce scheme that has not been tested under failover. Never reuse these keys, and never log epoch secrets or plaintext. RFC 10024 notes that its hybrid analysis relies on the TLS transcript, so do not assume this welcome construction is secure in other protocols without review. No agent is used: every verdict here is a deterministic audit.

checkYourself.q: Why is 'only the leader seals' an assumption of the term || counter nonce but not of random nonces?
checkYourself.a: Term || counter is unique because Raft gives at most one leader per term. Two sealers in one term would share a prefix and restart counters. Random nonces have no shared state, so any node may seal.

checkYourself.q: Why can't the outbox relay simply re-seal a stale-epoch envelope?
checkYourself.a: The outbox stores only sealed envelopes, so there is no plaintext on disk. The client resends after a 409.

checkYourself.q: Why must the dedupe table be replicated state rather than a cache on the API node?
checkYourself.a: A failover moves the API to a node that never saw the key. A re-sealed retry is a different ciphertext, so only the key in replicated state identifies the duplicate.

title: Quantum-safe migration: from Shor in a simulator to a crypto inventory
description: Run Shor's order finding for N = 15 and 21 on a statevector, put published RSA-2048 estimates next to it without extrapolating, inventory a sample codebase's public-key crypto, rank it with Mosca's inequality, and move one service to hybrid X25519MLKEM768 + ML-DSA-65 behind a registry with flag-driven rollout.
outcome: You can run and honestly scope a toy Shor experiment, build a code + config crypto inventory and a prioritised migration plan, migrate a service behind a crypto-agility port, and prove the seams with wire-level contract tests, fitness functions and a reproducible failure lab.
environment: Python 3.12 + numpy + cryptography 50.0.2 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA) on macOS (Apple silicon) or Windows 11; quantum topic's numpy statevector simulator (qsim) instead of hardware; Qiskit 2.x optional (CI cross-check).
overview: Migration to post-quantum cryptography fails at the joins between disciplines: a toy quantum result read as a timeline, an inventory finding no plan picks up, a service that looks migrated in code but negotiates X25519 on the wire.
This project wires three topics together and tests each join: quantum evidence -> risk model, inventory -> plan, agility layer <-> wire format, rollout flags <-> crypto policy.
prerequisites: quantum-computing L500 #25 (order finding, QFT) and L400 #19, #21
cryptography L400 #17 (crypto agility) and #18 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, hybrids)
application-architecture L200 #7 (ports and adapters) and L400 #20 (flags, fitness over time)
A venv with numpy and cryptography==50.0.2

designBrief.context: Six services and three config files use RSA, ECDH, ECDSA, X25519 and Ed25519. Messaging carries patient messages that must stay confidential for 12 years; traffic may be recorded today. Servers are upgraded one at a time, so v1 (X25519 only) and v2 servers coexist for weeks. Management asks 'when does RSA break - your simulator factored 21?'.
constraints: 0 claims about RSA-2048 that do not quote a published source; z (years to a CRQC) is a labelled assumption
inventory recall = precision = 1.0 against the hand-written ground truth (10 uses; docstrings and comments are not uses)
0 classical-only key exchanges for data with x + y > z outside a dated baseline
client first flight <= 1,400 B and handshake <= 6,144 B
0 algorithm names in service code; >= 1 registry resolution per handshake
0 classical sessions for messaging once pq_required is on, even with a v1 server left
every feature flag owned and not expired (fake clock 2026-10-30)
designBrief.question: In what order do we migrate, and how do we move messaging to a quantum-safe handshake through a crypto-agility layer and a mixed-version rollout - and prove it on the wire, not just in the code?

architecture.summary: shor_sim.py runs order finding on the quantum topic's qsim (12 and 15 qubits, compiled oracle, inverse QFT from L500 #25) and estimates.py holds only cited RSA-2048 estimates; both feed the risk model as evidence, never as z. inventory.py reuses quantum L400 #21's AST scanner plus config and registry-call rules over sample_repo/; migration_plan.py joins findings with services.json (x, y) and applies x + y > z against a labelled Horizon. The migrated messaging channel names no algorithm: it asks crypto_registry.py (policy + owned, expiring flags from app-arch L400 #20) for adapters (X25519, X25519MLKEM768 from cryptography L400 #18, Ed25519, ML-DSA-65/87, AES-256-GCM). fleet.py drives v1/v2 servers through four rollout phases while wire.Tap records every flight; seams.py and fitness.py judge the result and run_project.py prints the scorecard.

"""L600 #02 - Quantum-safe migration: from Shor in a simulator to a crypto inventory (end-to-end runner).

Run:  python run_project.py                    milestones, seams and fitness functions as JSON lines; exit 1 on any fail
      python run_project.py --inject bypass     failure lab: messaging's "fast path" skips the registry
      python run_project.py --inject downgrade  rollout fault: a compat shim re-adds X25519 when PQ is required
numpy + cryptography 50.0.2 + stdlib; Qiskit not needed (qsim statevector). Seeded; flags/baseline use a fake clock.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

import crypto_registry as registry
import estimates
import fitness
import fleet
import inventory
import migration_plan
import seams
import shor_sim
import wire

PHASES = [("all-v1", [1, 1, 1], False), ("mixed", [2, 2, 1], False), ("all-v2", [2, 2, 2], True),
          ("rollback-v1", [2, 2, 1], True)]          # last phase: one server rolled back while PQ is required


def collect(inject=None):
    sims = [shor_sim.shor(15, 7), shor_sim.shor(15, 7, gate_level=True), shor_sim.shor(21, 2)]
    expected = json.loads((registry.HERE / "EXPECTED_INVENTORY.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["before"]
    variant = inject or "migrated"
    folder = fleet.FOLDERS[variant]
    before, after = inventory.scan("before"), inventory.scan("after", messaging=folder)
    registry.reset()
    channel, phases, all_flights = fleet.load_channel(variant), {}, wire.Tap()
    for name, versions, required in PHASES:
        registry.AUDIT.clear()
        registry.FLAGS.set("pq_required.messaging", required)
        servers = fleet.make_fleet(versions)
        stats = fleet.run_traffic(channel, servers)
        stats.update(servers=servers, s3=seams.s3_agility_to_wire(stats["tap"]),
                     f3=fitness.f3_registry_only(registry.HERE / folder / "channel.py", stats["tap"]))
        all_flights.flights += stats["tap"].flights
        phases[name] = stats
    registry.reset()
    return {"sims": sims, "expected": expected, "before": before, "after": after, "phases": phases, "tap": all_flights}


def milestones(c):
    s15, s15g, s21 = c["sims"]
    score = inventory.score(c["before"], c["expected"])
    plan_b, plan_a = migration_plan.plan(c["before"]), migration_plan.plan(c["after"])
    msg_after = sorted({r["priority"] for r in plan_a if r["service"] == "messaging" and r["usage"] != "symmetric"})
    ph = c["phases"]
    sessions = {k: v["sessions"] for k, v in ph.items()}
    return [
        ("M1 Shor order finding on a statevector (N = 15, 21)",
         s15["factors"] == [3, 5] and s21["factors"] == [3, 7] and s15g["p_success_per_run"] == s15["p_success_per_run"]
         and all(shor_sim.matches_fft_shortcut(s) for s in c["sims"]),
         {f"N={s['N']}{' gate-level' if 'ccx' in s['gates'] else ''}": {"qubits": s["qubits"], "p_success": s["p_success_per_run"],
          "successes": f"{s['successes']}/{s['shots']}", "factors": s["factors"], "oracle_gates": {k: v for k, v in s["gates"].items()
          if k in ("cx", "ccx", "controlled_mult_permutations")}} for s in c["sims"]}),
        ("M2 published estimates, labelled", not estimates.check_claims(estimates.claims(c["sims"])),
         {"RSA-2048": {k: f"{v['physical_qubits']}, {v['runtime']}" for k, v in estimates.CITED.items()},
          "GE2019_formula_logical_qubits": estimates.ge_formula()["logical_qubits"],
          "NIST_IR_8547": estimates.NIST_IR_8547["timeline"]}),
        ("M3 crypto inventory (code + config)", score["recall"] == 1.0 and score["precision"] == 1.0,
         {"findings_before": len(c["before"]), "recall": score["recall"], "precision": score["precision"],
          "findings_after": len(c["after"])}),
        ("M4 Mosca risk + prioritised plan", migration_plan.summary(plan_b).get("P1") == 3 and msg_after == ["done"],
         {"z": migration_plan.HORIZON.z_years, "before": migration_plan.summary(plan_b), "after": migration_plan.summary(plan_a),
          "first_P1": f"{plan_b[0]['service']} {plan_b[0]['algorithm']} (x+y-z = {plan_b[0]['slack']})"}),
        ("M5 hybrid X25519MLKEM768 + ML-DSA-65 behind the registry, flag-driven rollout",
         ph["all-v2"]["sessions"] == {"X25519MLKEM768": 6} and ph["mixed"]["sessions"] == {"X25519MLKEM768": 4, "X25519": 2}
         and all(v["delivered"] + v["refused"] == 6 for v in ph.values()),
         {"sessions": sessions, "refused": {k: v["refused"] for k, v in ph.items()}}),
    ]


def seam_rows(c):
    ph = c["phases"]
    s3 = {k: v["s3"] for k, v in ph.items()}
    return [
        ("S1 quantum -> risk model: no extrapolation, z is a labelled assumption", seams.s1_quantum_to_risk(c["sims"])),
        ("S2 inventory -> plan: every finding owned and planned", seams.s2_inventory_to_plan(c["after"])),
        ("S3 agility layer <-> wire format: offers and sizes match the registry",
         {"ok": all(v["ok"] for v in s3.values()), **{k: v["problems"] or "ok" for k, v in s3.items()},
          "adapters_match_advertised": all(v["adapters_match_advertised"] for v in s3.values())}),
        ("S4 rollout flags <-> crypto policy: no downgrade when PQ is required",
         seams.s4_rollout_to_policy(ph["rollback-v1"], ph["rollback-v1"]["servers"])),
    ]


def fitness_rows(c):
    f3 = {k: v["f3"] for k, v in c["phases"].items()}
    return [
        ("F1 no classical-only key exchange for data with x + y > z (outside the dated baseline)",
         fitness.f1_no_classical_kex_for_exposed_data(c["after"])),
        ("F2 handshake byte budget", fitness.f2_handshake_budget(c["tap"])),
        ("F3 every service resolves algorithms via the registry",
         {"ok": all(v["ok"] for v in f3.values()), "static_violations": max(v["static_violations"] for v in f3.values()),
          "handshakes": sum(v["handshakes"] for v in f3.values()),
          "client_kex_resolutions": sum(v["client_kex_resolutions"] for v in f3.values())}),
        ("F4 feature flags owned and not expired", fitness.f4_flags_owned_and_live()),
    ]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=["bypass", "downgrade"])
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    c = collect(args.inject)
    passed = {"milestones": 0, "seams": 0, "fitness": 0}
    totals = {"milestones": 0, "seams": 0, "fitness": 0}
    for kind, rows in (("milestones", milestones(c)), ("seams", seam_rows(c)), ("fitness", fitness_rows(c))):
        for row in rows:
            name, ok, measure = (row[0], row[1], row[2]) if len(row) == 3 else (row[0], row[1]["ok"], row[1])
            measure = {k: v for k, v in measure.items() if k != "ok"}
            print(json.dumps({kind[:-1] if kind != "fitness" else "fitness": name, "pass": bool(ok), "measure": measure}))
            passed[kind] += bool(ok)
            totals[kind] += 1
    ok = passed == totals
    print(json.dumps({"scorecard": {k: f"{passed[k]}/{totals[k]}" for k in totals}, "inject": args.inject,
                      "all_pass": ok, "decided_by": "code"}))
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

inRealSystems: Crypto inventories for a PQC migration combine code and config scanning with runtime TLS telemetry, because the negotiated group shows what code scans miss.

IANA lists X25519MLKEM768 (0x11EC) as Recommended in the TLS Supported Groups registry (RFC 10024); servers that enable it next to X25519 face the same mixed-fleet negotiation as the rollout phases here.
Migration programmes rank systems by data lifetime and migration effort (Mosca), as NIST IR 8547 recommends for key establishment first.
useWhen: Use this pattern to plan and execute a PQC migration across many services: inventory, rank by HNDL exposure, migrate behind a registry with owned flags, and verify on the wire. Do not use the simulator to predict dates; do not deploy the lab's TLS-shaped protocol - use a real TLS 1.3 library.
simulatorVsReal: The quantum part runs a noiseless numpy statevector with compiled oracles (12-15 qubits); real factoring of RSA-2048 needs fault-tolerant machines estimated at < 1 million (2025) to 20 million (2019) noisy qubits under stated assumptions. The handshake is a TLS-shaped toy over in-process objects; RFC 10024 notes its security analysis relies on the real TLS 1.3 transcript.
caution: Never deploy the lab's wire format: the hybrid's security argument holds for TLS 1.3, not for home-made protocols (RFC 10024 sec. 6). Do not quote the toy N = 15/21 numbers as threat evidence. Keep classical fallback windows short, owned and expiring.

description: A tool-calling agent proposes screening runs and A/B experiments on the help-desk simulation and writes a summary. outcome: You can put an LLM agent in front of a stochastic simulator without letting it decide anything: arguments validated against a contract and an envelope, cost reserved before running, n chosen from statistics, every published number traced to a reproducible run, and overstated claims rejected.

overview: The agent may ask for any experiment and write any sentence; code decides what runs, how many times, at what cost, and which sentences anyone reads. The failure lab is the classic one: 'significant improvement' from 3 replications.

designBrief.context: A help desk (M/M/1, lam 0.8/min, mu 1.0/min, 30 tickets waiting on Monday) is considering a triage script that makes service 5% faster (mu 1.05). An agent plans the experiments and writes the report for the manager; a local model may hallucinate numbers and overstate results.
constraints: 100% of numeric claims in the published report trace to a registered run
every registered run reproduces bit-for-bit from its record (same environment fingerprint)
session budget 300,000 simulated customers and 8 model calls - never exceeded, reserved before running
'significant' only with >= 10 replications per arm and a 95% Welch CI of the difference that excludes 0; target half-width <= 0.3 min
proposals outside the schema or the verified envelope (lam/mu <= 0.9) never run and cost nothing
the model sees only the brief and tool results - no keys, no data files
designBrief.question: How do you let an agent drive simulation experiments while guaranteeing that every number and every 'significant' in its report is true?

architecture.summary: agent.py (ai-agents L100 #6 loop, L300 #14 Budget) sends tool calls to a job pipeline. contract.py validates them with the ai-agents L200 #8 validator against the same schemas the model receives, plus the envelope rule lam/mu <= 0.9 (verified in M1). SimBudget reserves cost in simulated customers before any run. pipeline.py runs the simulation L200 #10 help desk with seeds keyed by SeedSequence(root, spawn_key=(arm, rep)) and the L300 #14 Morris code through an adapter, sizes replications with solution/replications.py, and writes runs and experiment facts to an append-only JSONL registry (run_id = sha256 of model, version, params, seed; value as float.hex). claims.py checks every summary sentence against the cited experiment's facts and verdict; rejected sentences are replaced by code-written lines. run_project.py prints a JSON-lines scorecard: 5 milestones, 4 seams, 3 fitness functions.

"""L600 #03: an AI agent that runs simulation experiments - and can't fool you.

The agent (a tool-calling loop) proposes screening runs and A/B experiments on the L200 #10 help-desk simulation and
writes a summary. Code decides everything else: the contract gate (schema + verified envelope), the budget gate,
seeded runs into an append-only registry, replications sized from a target CI half-width, and a claim check of
every sentence. Prints one JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function; exits 1 on any failure.
python run_project.py [--inject few-reps|unseeded|no-contract|no-budget-gate] [--real-model]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import agent
import claims
import model
import pipeline
import registry as reg
import stats

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = HERE / "out"
BRIEF = ("Help-desk study, seed 13. Screen with sobol 64. Screen with morris 10. "
         "Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.8 with 3 replications. Compare mu 1.0 vs 1.05 at lam 0.97 with 3 replications.")
SIM_BUDGET, HALF_WIDTH, MAX_CALLS = 300_000, 0.3, 8  # customers per session; min; agent model calls
FAULTS = ("few-reps", "unseeded", "no-contract", "no-budget-gate")


def verify_model():
    """M1 (L100 #6 V&V): 95% CI of 10 long runs must cover the M/M/1 formula; same seed -> same bits."""
    rows = []
    for rho in (0.5, 0.8, 0.9):
        p = {"lam": rho, "mu": 1.0, "backlog": 0, "customers": 20_000, "warmup": 2_000}
        m, h = stats.mean_ci([model.run_once(p, model.seed_for(6, 0, r)) for r in range(10)])
        rows.append({"rho": rho, "sim": round(m, 3), "half_width": round(h, 3), "formula": round(model.mm1_wq(rho, 1.0), 3),
                     "covered": abs(m - model.mm1_wq(rho, 1.0)) <= h})
    p = {"lam": 0.8, "mu": 1.0}
    same = model.run_once(p, 123).hex() == model.run_once(p, 123).hex()
    return rows, same


def session(inject, real_model, registry):
    pl = pipeline.Pipeline(registry, pipeline.SimBudget(SIM_BUDGET, gate=inject != "no-budget-gate"),
                           half_width=HALF_WIDTH, policy=pipeline.naive_policy if inject == "few-reps" else None,
                           gate=inject != "no-contract", seeded=inject != "unseeded")
    server = None
    if real_model:
        url, name = os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL_URL", "http://localhost:11434/v1"), os.environ.get("LOCAL_MODEL", "qwen2.5:1.5b")
    else:
        import fake_sim_agent
        (server, url), name = fake_sim_agent.start_in_thread(), "fake-model"
    try:
        out = agent.run_session(BRIEF, pl, url, name, max_calls=MAX_CALLS)
    finally:
        if server:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
    return pl, out


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=FAULTS)
    ap.add_argument("--real-model", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    out_dir = args.out
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out_dir / "registry.jsonl").unlink(missing_ok=True)  # fresh registry per run (append-only within a run)
    registry = reg.Registry(out_dir / "registry.jsonl")
    lines = []

    def score(kind, name, passed, **measures):
        lines.append({kind: name, "pass": bool(passed), **measures})
        print(json.dumps(lines[-1]))

    v_rows, same = verify_model()
    pl, out = session(args.inject, args.real_model, registry)
    rows, published = claims.review(out["summary"], registry)
    rejected_jobs = [j for j in pl.jobs if j["states"][-1] == "REJECTED"]
    by_contract = [j["job"] for j in rejected_jobs if "VALIDATED" not in j["states"]]
    by_budget = [j["job"] for j in rejected_jobs if "VALIDATED" in j["states"]]
    runs_rejected = sum(r["job"] in by_contract + by_budget for r in registry.runs())
    outside = [j["job"] for j in pl.jobs if j["tool"] == "run_experiment" and "RAN" in j["states"]
               and max(j["args"][a]["lam"] / j["args"][a]["mu"] for a in ("baseline", "candidate")) > 0.9]
    exps = [r for r in registry.records if r["kind"] == "experiment" and "verdict" in r["facts"]]
    ab = {k: v["value"] for k, v in exps[0]["facts"].items()} if exps else {}
    hw = ab.get("difference_half_width", float("inf"))
    run_ids = registry.run_ids()
    facts_ok = all(set(f["runs"]) <= run_ids for e in registry.records if e["kind"] == "experiment" for f in e["facts"].values())
    repro = [reg.reproduce(r) for r in registry.runs()]
    found, traced = claims.traced_runs(published, registry)
    recheck = [r for r in claims.review(published, registry)[0] if not r["ok"]]
    overclaim = [r["sentence"] for r in rows if "significan" in r["sentence"] and not r["ok"]]

    score("milestone", "M1 model verified (V&V) + reproducible", all(r["covered"] for r in v_rows) and same,
          checks=v_rows, same_seed_same_bits=same, model=f"{model.NAME}@{model.VERSION}")
    score("milestone", "M2 contract gate before any run", bool(by_contract) and not outside and not runs_rejected,
          rejected_by_contract=by_contract, ran_outside_envelope=outside, runs_for_rejected_jobs=runs_rejected)
    score("milestone", "M3 experiment registry", len(repro) > 0 and facts_ok and all(repro),
          runs=len(repro), experiments=len([r for r in registry.records if r["kind"] == "experiment"]),
          facts_trace_to_runs=facts_ok)
    score("milestone", "M4 replications from target half-width", hw <= HALF_WIDTH and ab.get("replications", 0) >= 10,
          requested=3, replications=ab.get("replications"), diff_half_width=round(hw, 3), target=HALF_WIDTH,
          verdict=ab.get("verdict"), diff=round(ab.get("difference", 0), 3))
    score("milestone", "M5 claim check + published report", bool(rows) and not recheck,
          sentences=len(rows), rejected=[{"sentence": r["sentence"][:60], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in rows if not r["ok"]])
    score("seam", "agent <-> tool schema", bool(by_contract) and not outside, test="tests/test_seam_contract.py")
    score("seam", "agent claims <-> computed statistics", not recheck and all(not r["ok"] for r in rows
          if r["sentence"].startswith("At lam")), test="tests/test_seam_claims.py")
    score("seam", "sim stochasticity <-> conclusions", ab.get("verdict") != "inconclusive" and hw <= HALF_WIDTH
          and not overclaim, verdict=ab.get("verdict"), overclaims_rejected=overclaim, test="tests/test_seam_replications.py")
    score("seam", "cost/time budget", pl.budget.spent <= SIM_BUDGET and out["calls"] <= MAX_CALLS
          and not runs_rejected, rejected_by_budget=by_budget, spent=pl.budget.spent, limit=SIM_BUDGET, agent_calls=out["calls"], ledger=pl.budget.ledger,
          test="tests/test_seam_budget.py")
    score("fitness", "100% of numeric claims traced to a registry run", found > 0 and traced == found,
          numbers=found, traced=traced, test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_claims_traced")
    score("fitness", "every run reproducible bit-for-bit from its seed", repro and all(repro),
          reproduced=sum(repro), runs=len(repro), env=model.ENVIRONMENT, test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_runs_reproducible")
    score("fitness", "budget never exceeded", pl.budget.spent <= SIM_BUDGET
          and sum(a for _, a in pl.budget.ledger) == pl.budget.spent, spent=pl.budget.spent, limit=SIM_BUDGET,
          test="tests/test_fitness.py::test_budget_never_exceeded")
    passed = sum(x["pass"] for x in lines)
    final = {"scorecard": "PASS" if passed == len(lines) else "FAIL", "passed": passed, "total": len(lines),
             "inject": args.inject}
    print(json.dumps(final))
    registry.close()
    (out_dir / "scorecard.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(x) + "\n" for x in lines + [final]), encoding="utf-8")
    (out_dir / "report.md").write_text(f"# Published summary\n\n{published}\n\n# Agent draft\n\n{out['summary']}\n",
                                   encoding="utf-8")
    return 0 if final["scorecard"] == "PASS" else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

glossary.meaning: Write locally first (flash log); the network only drains the log. A sync deletes only what was acknowledged.
(device, boot, seq): a unique, immutable identity per reading. seq restarts per boot; boot is persisted in flash.
A state-based CRDT that ships only the part of its state a peer lacks; merge is still a join (Almeida et al.).
Compact causal context: contiguous high-water mark per (device, boot) plus the dots received above it.
Ack that names exact records stored above the contiguous mark, so a permanent gap cannot block later deletes.
Each node regularly picks a random peer and both swap what the other lacks (Demers et al.).
First byte of every radio frame: selects the record layout (1 = 8 B, 2 = 9 B).
Readings at or below the contiguous mark: final, so an API can page through them with a cursor.

concepts: Integration fails at the seams: give each a contract, a fault and a test.
Identity is not time: dots survive reboots and clock steps; wall time is data.
Ship deltas that fit the link; merge with a join so loss and duplicates only delay.
Contracts check shape; a fitness function checks completeness.

designBrief.context: A school wants 20 battery-powered micro:bits around the building reporting temperature and light every minute to a backend with a dashboard API. Radio coverage is patchy (30 % loss, a wing out of range for hours), gateways are ordinary PCs that crash, drift and get cut off, boards reboot, and four boards will run old firmware for months. Simulator only; one seeded run must be reproducible on a Mac mini and a Windows PC.
constraints: 0 readings lost under 30 % per-delivery loss, 5 % duplicates, 5 % reordering, a 3-hour radio partition, a 4-hour gateway partition and a 1-hour gateway crash
every radio frame <= the configured radio length (32 B default); 0 frames rejected
replicas agree within 4 push-pull gossip rounds once writes stop
modelled battery life >= 2,000 h per board at the chosen sync interval (microbit L300 #14 figures)
a schema-1 board appears in /v2 with "schema": 1 and "light": null; /v1 keeps working with Deprecation + Sunset
a client paging /v2 readings never skips a reading that arrives late
designBrief.question: Which identity, sync protocol, merge and API contract keep every reading - and how do you prove each seam separately?

architecture.summary: Each board appends readings to a flash log (dot = dev, boot, seq), and every 10 samples it turns the radio on. It sends only unacked records, three per 30-byte frame, then turns the radio off again. Two gateways decode frames by the schema byte, store them in a durable dot store and ack (boot, contiguous mark) plus the exact dots stored above it. Gateways and three backend replicas run push-pull anti-entropy every 5 minutes. They swap deltas computed from each other's digest (version vector + dot cloud). Replica b1 serves /v1 (deprecated) and /v2, which pages only the stable prefix. Two dashboards publish consumer contracts that the provider verifies against the live API.

seams.between: microbit ↔ distributed-systems (radio length ↔ CRDT state size)
seams.contract: device→gateway traffic is a delta: unacked records only, 3 B header + 3 x 9 B <= radio length 32; a body that is not a whole number of records is rejected
seams.risk: a state-based sync (one board's 12 h log = 6,480 B = 224 frames) or frames sized for 251 B with the radio left at 32 B are silently truncated by the sender: --inject oversize-frame loses 14,082 of 14,400

seams.between: microbit ↔ distributed-systems (device clock ↔ identity and order)
seams.contract: a reading's identity is its dot (dev, boot, seq); per-device order is (boot, seq); device wall time is only an attribute
seams.risk: running_time() restarts at 0 on reboot and acks from a slow gateway step the epoch back: 1,421 (device, wall-second) keys repeat; a store keyed by them loses exactly those readings

seams.contract: the device starts every sync (Deep Sleep cannot receive), every SYNC_EVERY samples, <= 3 attempts with a 50 ms ack window; awake time is costed with budget.FIGURES
seams.risk: frequent or retry-heavy syncs drain the battery; rare syncs need per-sync capacity above the backlog or the flash log overflows

seams.contract: schema byte selects the layout (1: 8 B, 2: 9 B); firmware and gateway tables equal; /v2 returns schema and light null for schema 1
seams.risk: a gateway assuming the newest layout rejects every schema-1 frame: --inject schema-drift never acks 2,880 readings and breaks 7 contract checks

seams.contract: /v2/devices/{dev}/readings serves only seq <= the version-vector mark of that boot (stableThrough); latest = max (boot, seq)
seams.risk: serving the dot cloud lets a cursor pass seq 3 before gossip delivers it - the client never sees it

failureLab.inject: python run_project.py --inject wallclock-lww (or FLEET_STORE=lww for the test). Gateways and replicas store readings as rows keyed (device, device wall second), last write wins (distributed-systems L400 #18 LWWRegister), as a time-series table does with a duplicate key. The fault exists only because the topics meet. A micro:bit's running_time() restarts at 0 on reboot (d07 at minute 300). Its wall time is built from the epoch in the last gateway ack, and g2's clock is 300 s slow. A backend that trusts that time as a key overwrites readings.
failureLab.symptom: Scorecard FAIL 9/12, exit 1: S2 {wall_key_repeats: 1421, lost: 1421}, F1 lost 1421, S4 2,670 of 2,880 schema-1 rows. M2 still says every reading reached a gateway and the logs are empty, M4's contracts pass, and the replicas converge - on the wrong data.
failureLab.diagnose: Compare sampled dots with stored dots per device: the losses are on d07 after its reboot and on boards that heard g2. Count repeated (device, wall second) pairs in the sampled data: 1,421, exactly the loss. The gateway acked each reading, so the device deleted it, and a later reading with the same key overwrote it.
failureLab.fix: Key by the dot (dev, boot, seq), with boot persisted in flash and one write per boot. Merge as a grow-only map with a version vector plus dot cloud. Keep wall time as a display attribute. Order per device by (boot, seq) (ADR 0001).

scalingLimits: Partitions longer than the flash log: 400 records = 6.7 h at one per minute. Signal: dropped_flash_full > 0 and peak_log = MAX_LOG (try it 2: 8 h -> 451 dropped, 450 lost). After that the board's /v2 stableThrough stops at the gap, because a dropped seq never arrives.

Radio airtime and collisions are not modelled. With hundreds of boards per gateway, signal: attempts per sync rise and p95 time-to-gateway grows even without partitions. Stagger the syncs, add listen-before-talk or more gateways and channels.

Digest size grows with (device x boot) entries and with gaps in the dot cloud. Signal: gossip bytes per round grow with fleet size even when nothing changed. Shard digests per device range or use Merkle trees.

TARGET_LIFE_H = 2000         # one school term on 2 x AAA (model, not a measurement)
MAX_ROUNDS = 4               # gossip rounds for 5 replicas to agree
RADIO_LENGTH = 32


def get(url):
    with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=5) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8")), dict(resp.headers)


def api_walk(url, store):
    """Page every device/boot through /v2 readings; the sum must equal the store (no gaps, no repeats)."""
    total = 0
    for dev, boot in sorted({(d[0], d[1]) for d in store.dots()}):
        after = 0
        while True:
            page, _ = get("%s/v2/devices/d%02d/readings?boot=%d&after=%d&limit=500" % (url, dev, boot, after))
            total += len(page["items"])
            if page["next"] is None:
                break
            after = page["next"]
    return total


def api_and_contracts(store):
    paths, tiles = contracts.consumer_side()
    with api.serve(store) as url:
        problems = contracts.verify(url)
        try:
            _, headers = get(url + "/v1/devices/d01/latest")
        except OSError:
            headers = {}
        return problems, tiles, headers.get("Deprecation"), api_walk(url, store)


def scorecard(r, law, conv, problems, deprecation, walked):
    fw = r["boards"][0].lab
    v1_rows = [d for d, v in r["stores"]["b1"].rows() if v[3] == 1]
    n_bad = sum(len(p) for p in problems.values())
    full_state_frames = -(-720 * fw.REC_LEN[2] // (RADIO_LENGTH - fw.HEADER))
    budget = _kb.budget()
    return [
        ("milestone", "M1 offline-first devices", {"sampled": r["sampled"], "dropped": r["dropped_flash_full"],
         "peak_log": r["peak_log"]}, "14400 sampled, 0 dropped, peak <= %d" % fw.MAX_LOG,
         r["sampled"] == 14400 and r["dropped_flash_full"] == 0 and r["peak_log"] <= fw.MAX_LOG),
        ("milestone", "M2 delta sync over a lossy radio", {"reached_gateway": r["reached_gateway"], "tries":
         r["tries"], "frames": r["frames"], "logs_empty": r["logs_empty"]}, "every reading at a gateway; logs empty",
         r["reached_gateway"] == r["sampled"] and r["logs_empty"]),
        ("milestone", "M3 CRDT merge + gossip", {"laws": "%d/%d" % (law["passed"], law["trials"]),
         "replicas_equal": r["replicas_equal"], "wrong_values": r["wrong_values"]}, "laws all pass; 5 replicas equal",
         law["passed"] == law["trials"] and r["replicas_equal"] and r["wrong_values"] == 0),
        ("milestone", "M4 versioned API + contracts", {"contract_problems": n_bad, "v1_deprecation": deprecation,
         "api_rows": walked}, "0 problems; v1 deprecated; API rows == stored", n_bad == 0 and bool(deprecation)
         and walked == r["stored_b1"]),
        ("seam", "S1 radio length <-> CRDT delta size", {"max_frame_bytes": r["max_frame_bytes"], "rejected":
         r["rejected"], "full_state_frames_per_device": full_state_frames}, "frames <= %d B, 0 rejected" %
         RADIO_LENGTH, r["max_frame_bytes"] <= RADIO_LENGTH and sum(r["rejected"].values()) == 0),
        ("seam", "S2 device clock <-> identity/order", {"wall_key_repeats": r["wall_key_repeats"], "lost":
         r["lost"]}, "repeats exist, 0 lost", r["wall_key_repeats"] > 0 and r["lost"] == 0),
        ("seam", "S3 battery <-> sync interval", {"firmware_active_ms": fw.ACTIVE_MS, "model_active_ms":
         budget.FIGURES["ACTIVE_MS"], "life_h_min": r["life_h_min"]}, "same ACTIVE_MS; life >= %d h" %
         TARGET_LIFE_H, fw.ACTIVE_MS == budget.FIGURES["ACTIVE_MS"] and r["life_h_min"] >= TARGET_LIFE_H),
        ("seam", "S4 firmware schema <-> backend contract", {"schema1_rows": len(v1_rows), "rec_len_equal":
         fw.REC_LEN == gateway.REC_LEN}, "2880 schema-1 rows; layouts equal", len(v1_rows) == 2880 and
         fw.REC_LEN == gateway.REC_LEN),
        ("seam", "S5 CRDT state <-> API paging", {"api_rows": walked, "stored": r["stored_b1"]},
         "paged rows == stored", walked == r["stored_b1"]),
        ("fitness", "F1 zero lost readings (30% loss + partitions)", {"lost": r["lost"], "sampled": r["sampled"]},
         "lost == 0", r["lost"] == 0 and r["wrong_values"] == 0),
        ("fitness", "F2 convergence within N gossip rounds", {"end_of_run": r["convergence_rounds"],
         "experiment_max": conv["max"], "experiment_mean": conv["mean"]}, "<= %d rounds" % MAX_ROUNDS,
         r["convergence_rounds"] <= MAX_ROUNDS and conv["max"] <= MAX_ROUNDS),
        ("fitness", "F3 battery life at the chosen sync interval", {"sync_every_min": fw.SYNC_EVERY,
         "life_h_min": r["life_h_min"]}, ">= %d h" % TARGET_LIFE_H, r["life_h_min"] >= TARGET_LIFE_H),
    ]


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=fleet_sim.INJECTS)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=4)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    r = fleet_sim.run(seed=args.seed, inject=args.inject)
    problems, tiles, deprecation, walked = api_and_contracts(r["stores"]["b1"])
    rows = scorecard(r, laws.check(args.seed), fleet_sim.convergence_experiment(seed=args.seed), problems,
                     deprecation, walked)
    for kind, name, value, threshold, ok in rows:
        print(json.dumps({"kind": kind, "check": name, "value": value, "threshold": threshold, "pass": bool(ok)}))
    passed = sum(bool(row[-1]) for row in rows)
    print(json.dumps({"scorecard": "PASS" if passed == len(rows) else "FAIL", "passed": passed, "total": len(rows),
                      "seed": args.seed, "inject": args.inject, "dashboard": tiles[:3]}))
    return 0 if passed == len(rows) else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

inRealSystems: InfluxDB identifies a point by measurement, tag set and timestamp, and a duplicate point takes the new field values - the failure lab's last-writer-wins by timestamp. Its docs suggest a unique tag or timestamp nudge; this lab uses a dot.

Delta-state CRDTs with a compact causal context (version vector + dot cloud) are specified by Almeida, Shoker and Baquero; this lab's ReadingStore is the simplest member: a grow-only map of immutable readings.
Anti-entropy by random peer exchange was implemented in Xerox's Clearinghouse servers (Demers et al. 1987), which reported it solved long-standing database inconsistency there.
HTTP APIs announce deprecation with Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers and protect consumers with consumer-driven contracts (e.g. Pact).
useWhen: Use this shape when devices that sleep, reboot and lose packets feed a replicated backend that other teams read through an API. Give readings an identity that never depends on a clock, ship deltas that fit the link, merge with a join, version the device schema and the API separately, and test every seam on its own line.
simulatorVsReal: Device parts are validated-stub: the firmware runs on the microbit topic's CPython stub (no MicroPython VM, no real timing). The radio stub has seeded per-delivery loss, duplicates and reordering, but no airtime, collisions, range or length-dependent loss. The flash log is a dict (a file on a board, with flash wear not modelled). Battery hours are the microbit L300 #14 model, with an assumed 0.5 mA sleep floor and an assumed 50 ms ack window, not measurements. Gateways and replicas run in one process with simulated partitions. The official micro:bit V2 simulator run is pendingCi.
caution: The API binds 127.0.0.1 only and has no authentication. Do not expose it, and add auth before real use (application-architecture L200 #10). Radio frames here are unauthenticated: anyone in range can forge a reading (see microbit L400 #19 for authenticated frames). Classroom sensor data can reveal occupancy patterns, so keep it on site (microbit L500 #26).

checkYourself.q: Why did the LWW store lose readings that every gateway had acknowledged?
checkYourself.a: The ack was correct, because the gateway received the reading. The row key (device, wall second) repeated after d07's reboot and after acks from the slow g2. A later write with the same key replaced the row. Identity must not depend on a clock (ADR 0001).

checkYourself.q: Why does a device need selective acks if gateways already ack a contiguous mark?
checkYourself.a: A record dropped from a full log never arrives, so the mark stops at the gap forever and nothing above it is ever deleted. Exact acks let the board free what is stored. Without them an 8 h partition lost 2,330 readings instead of 450.

checkYourself.q: Contracts passed in the failure lab. Were they wrong?
checkYourself.a: No: they check shape and the schema seam. Completeness is a fitness function (F1) comparing sampled dots with stored dots.

checkYourself.q: Why serve only the contiguous prefix in /v2 readings?
checkYourself.a: Gossip delivers dots out of order. A cursor that passed seq 4 would never return for a late seq 3. Below the mark nothing can arrive later.

title: A robotic-observatory night scheduler
description: Schedule one night for a small robotic telescope: astronomy constraints (airmass, twilight, Moon) through a typed UTC seam, a greedy baseline vs a seeded local search, 1000 Markov-cloud nights to price every promise, and a local model that proposes and explains while a deterministic validator decides.
outcome: You can build a constrained night scheduler whose every boundary is guarded: typed UTC instants into sky maths, an independent validator for any plan (including an agent's), weather-aware promises checked by simulation, and fitness functions that keep the design true.

Astronomy decides what is observable, simulation decides what a plan is worth under clouds, and a local model may only propose and explain. The interesting failures live at the seams between them, so every seam has a test.

designBrief.context: A 0.4 m robotic telescope at Gurgaon (28.46 N, 77.03 E, IST = UTC+05:30) has one night (2026-11-19, waxing gibbous Moon) and 11 observation requests with priorities 1-5 and uninterrupted exposures of 30-180 minutes. The site loses time to cloud spells. A local model is available to draft plans and explain them to observers.
constraints: no scheduled observation above airmass 2.0, below the horizon, outside astronomical darkness (Sun <= -18 deg) or within 30 deg of the Moon, re-checked every 5 minutes by an independent route
expected completed priority-weighted value >= 1.15 x the greedy baseline over 1000 seeded weather runs, with the paired 95 % CI of the difference above 0
the same seed gives the same schedule (plan hash) and the same weather runs
every promise (p_complete per block) within 3 binomial standard errors of its simulated completion rate
no plan from the local model is executed unless it passes the validator and promises at least the optimiser's value
designBrief.question: Which scheduler should run tonight, what may it promise each observer, and how do we stop a time-zone or agent mistake from pointing the telescope below the horizon?

architecture.summary: timeutil.UtcInstant is the only time that reaches sky.py, which turns astronomy L300 #12's ephemeris and Kasten & Young airmass into 64 ten-minute dark slots and a feasibility matrix. scheduler.py runs a greedy dispatcher and a seeded local search over request order (earliest-fit decoder) that maximises the expected value from weather.py's two-state Markov cloud model. validator.py re-derives altitude from astronomy L100 #3's apparent sidereal time every 5 minutes and judges every plan; weather.py replays 1000 nights with common random numbers to check the promises; agent_plan.py turns a local model's PLAN lines into typed rows for the same validator and gates its explanation. run_project.py prints one JSON line per milestone, seam and fitness function.

seams.contract: sky functions accept only UtcInstant (aware, offset 0, built by astimezone); local time exists only for display; sidereal time in hours, RA in degrees
seams.risk: a local wall clock read as UTC moves the sky 330 minutes: the scheduler's own airmass column still looks fine (1.982) while Betelgeuse is at -16.4 deg

seams.contract: model text -> 'PLAN <target> <ISO 8601 with Z or offset>' -> UtcInstant rows -> validator.validate(); adopt only with 0 violations and expected value >= the optimiser's; explanation numbers must be facts
seams.risk: an unzoned time is guessed, a below-horizon block is executed, or an invented number reaches an observer

seams.contract: the scheduler promises p_complete = pi (1 - a)^(n-1) per block and sum(priority x p) per plan; 1000 SeedSequence-child nights must reproduce both
seams.risk: nominal priority sums or independent-slot weather over-promise long blocks; an unpaired comparison hides a real difference in noise

seams.between: astronomy ↔ validator (units: degrees / hours / radians / minutes)
seams.contract: *_deg, *_h and *_min in names; LST hours x 15 -> degrees; radians only inside trig; exposures whole 10-min slots
seams.risk: a dropped x 15 or radians-as-degrees moves stars by tens of degrees without any exception

failureLab.symptom: The scheduler is happy: its own rows report max airmass 1.982. The independent validator is not: 'Betelgeuse: altitude -16.4 deg, airmass inf at 2026-11-19T13:20:00Z'. Scorecard 7/12, exit 1 (M2, M3, M5, SEAM time, FF1 fail).
failureLab.diagnose: Compare sky_instant(slot) with slot.utc: they differ by exactly 330 minutes, the IST offset. The scheduler computed the sky 5 h 30 min after the instant it published. Type checks passed because a relabelled clock has offset 0.
failureLab.fix: Sky maths accepts only UtcInstant; build it with UtcInstant.from_aware() (astimezone), never replace(tzinfo=UTC); a lint-style test forbids that pattern outside the marked fault line; the seam test re-validates every block at its published UTC time by an independent sidereal route.

scalingLimits: More requests, nights or telescopes: order search over requests x slots x sites loses quality and time; signal: the plan changes with the seed or the search stops improving long before its move budget. Move to ILP/CP (as Las Cumbres did) and keep the validator as the judge.
Real weather is not one stationary chain: realised completion rates fall outside the promised 3-sigma band night after night. Fit a and b per season from site logs and re-plan on live cloud data.

Low-precision ephemeris (J2000 without precession, about 0.36 deg by 2026; low-precision Moon): fine at airmass 2, not at a tight limit; signal: blocks within 0.5 deg of a limit disagree with astropy/astroplan (pendingCi).

codeWalkthrough.title: timeutil.UtcInstant
codeWalkthrough.detail: Frozen dataclass; __post_init__ refuses naive datetimes and non-zero offsets; from_aware() converts with astimezone(). lst_hours() reuses astronomy L100 #3's GAST.

codeWalkthrough.title: sky.feasibility()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Kasten & Young airmass and Moon separation at every 10-min boundary; ok[i, s] only if the whole block (n + 1 boundaries) passes. sky_instant() holds the injectable fault.

codeWalkthrough.title: scheduler.greedy()
codeWalkthrough.detail: At each free slot, the highest-priority feasible request (ties: airmass, name). Taking Deneb at dusk loses Vega - the myopia the local search fixes.

codeWalkthrough.title: scheduler.decode() + local_search()
codeWalkthrough.detail: An order becomes a plan by earliest fit; 3000 seeded swap/move proposals, accept if not worse, starting from greedy's order so the result is never below the baseline.

codeWalkthrough.title: weather.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Two-state Markov clouds, one SeedSequence child per run, all-or-nothing blocks; expected() is the analytic promise, realised() the simulated payout, summary() the simulation topic's t-interval.

codeWalkthrough.title: validator.validate()
codeWalkthrough.detail: Independent sidereal route, 5-min samples, Sun, Moon, grid, overlap, duplicates; returns reasons and never repairs.

codeWalkthrough.title: agent_plan.py + run_project.py
codeWalkthrough.detail: Fake-model rules registered at runtime; PLAN lines parsed to UtcInstant; decide() adopts only a valid, at-least-as-good plan; explanations gated by numbers and names. run_project prints the scorecard and exits 1 on any FAIL.

inRealSystems: Las Cumbres Observatory schedules its global telescope network from observation requests with an integer linear program (Lampoudi, Saunders & Eastman 2015) and re-schedules as conditions change.

astroplan (Astropy affiliated) expresses the same constraints (AtNightConstraint, AirmassConstraint, MoonSeparationConstraint) and offers sequential and priority schedulers - the library equivalent of sky.py + scheduler.py.
Weather generators in hydrology and agriculture use first-order two-state Markov chains for wet/dry occurrence since Gabriel & Neumann (1962).
useWhen: Use this shape whenever an optimiser plans against physical constraints and an uncertain environment and someone wants an AI to help: type the time and unit seams, judge every plan with an independent validator, price promises by simulation, and keep the model at the edge.
simulatorVsReal: No telescope or weather station: the sky comes from low-precision ephemerides (about 1-2 arcmin Sun/Moon, J2000 targets), clouds from an assumed Markov chain, and the agent from a deterministic fake model. A real deployment adds slews, filter changes, calibration frames, live cloud sensors and re-planning during the night.
caution: Planning and teaching only. Never let a model command hardware or bypass the validator; never put credentials, site network details or personal data in prompts. Weather parameters are assumptions - fit them to your site before promising anyone anything.

checkYourself.q: Why does a relabelled local time pass the UtcInstant type check?
checkYourself.a: replace(tzinfo=UTC) produces an aware datetime with offset 0 - a valid UtcInstant for the wrong instant. Only the independent re-validation at the published time catches it.

checkYourself.q: Why can the optimiser's mean advantage grow at a cloudier site while greedy wins more nights?
checkYourself.a: The optimiser avoids long risky blocks, which matters more when clouds are common (ratio 1.325), but the night-to-night spread also grows, so greedy's plan wins 23 % of single nights.

checkYourself.q: What stops an agent plan with a good-looking WHY line from being executed?
checkYourself.a: decide() never reads the WHY line: it parses PLAN lines into UtcInstant rows, runs the validator and compares expected value.

title: A verifiable, replicated science-data release pipeline
description: Process Gaia-like astrometry into distances, publish it as a canonical, Merkle-hashed, dual-signed release, replicate it to 4 mirrors by anti-entropy, and let an untrusting client verify signatures, hashes, licence, log proofs and freshness.
outcome: You can build a release pipeline where any mirror may lag or lie and a client still gets the newest authentic data or a clear refusal - and you can name, test and fix the four seams where the three topics meet.
environment: Python 3.12 (validated on 3.12, Linux x86_64) + numpy + cryptography 50.0.2 (Ed25519, ML-DSA-65, SHA-256); stdlib unittest; imports astronomy L100 #4 + L400 #21, cryptography L200 #7 + L300 #14 + L400 #17 and distributed-systems L400 #17 via _kb.py. Optional: minisign 0.12, CyberChef (manual checks).
overview: A science release is only useful if anyone can prove, years later and from any mirror, that the bytes are the ones the team signed, under the licence the inputs require, and that nothing newer was hidden. This project wires an astronomy processing step to a cryptographic release format and a gossiping mirror network, then breaks the joints on purpose: a mirror that re-serialises floats, a rotation that forgets old keys, a client that trusts stale mirrors, a builder that drops Gaia's NonCommercial term.
prerequisites: Astronomy L100 #4 (parallax, distance modulus) and L400 #21 (licences, citation, manifests)
Cryptography L200 #7 (Ed25519), L300 #14 (signed manifests) and L400 #17 (dual signing, registry)
Distributed systems L400 #17 (seeded event simulation, staleness) and L400 #18 (merge laws)

designBrief.context: A small team publishes a derived catalogue (synthetic Gaia-like astrometry -> distances) every 20 minutes of simulated time. Four volunteer mirrors serve it; one stores uploads in a JSON document store, one is regularly partitioned. Users verify with their own tools, in several languages, and cite exact versions for years.
constraints: any single-byte change in any release object is detected: 100 % of 15,586 single-bit flips
4 mirrors converge within 4 gossip rounds of 60 s after the last one becomes reachable
a client never accepts a release older than the newest it has seen, nor an expired timestamp
old releases still verify after a key rotation; a retired key cannot sign a new version
Gaia's CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO terms and credit survive: release CC-BY-NC-4.0, credit verbatim and signed
runs offline in minutes with seeded data and a fake clock; no secrets leave the machine
designBrief.question: Where must the boundaries between the science code, the crypto and the mirror network be made explicit - and how do we test each one?

architecture.summary: science.py turns astronomy L400 #21 rows into distances (inverse parallax only when parallax/error >= 5). publisher.py runs the licence gate, writes 5 files as RFC 8785 (JCS) bytes, builds a manifest with SHA-256 + length per file and an RFC 9162 Merkle root, signs it with Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 (crypto L400 #17 registry), appends its hash to a transparency log and issues a 1-hour timestamp. Only mirror m0 receives the upload; mirrors.py spreads it by push-pull gossip that compares a Merkle tree over 16 key buckets (distributed L400 #17's Sim drives the rounds). client.py trusts one root.json, follows the root chain, checks timestamp expiry and version monotonicity, the release signatures inside each key's validity window, every file, the Merkle root, the licence and attribution, and the log's inclusion and consistency proofs.

seams.contract: Hashes and signatures cover RFC 8785 (JCS) bytes of the catalogue; every re-serialisation is idempotent; the client parses strictly (bytes must equal the JCS form of their content).
seams.risk: A stack that writes doubles with '%.17g' (or Python's 5.0 / 2.5e-05 layout) produces the same values in different bytes: hashes differ, mirrors never converge, cross-language verifiers fail.

seams.contract: Mirrors keep every old release forever, so root.json keeps retired release keys with valid_through_version; root N+1 needs signatures from root N and N+1.
seams.risk: A rotation that drops old keys makes every mirrored v1-v3 unverifiable; keeping them fully trusted lets a stolen retired key sign v5.

seams.contract: A timestamp (version + expiry, TTL 3600 s) pins the newest release; the client never goes below the highest version seen; TTL > re-sign interval + replication lag + skew.
seams.risk: A lagging or frozen mirror serves validly signed but old data (rollback / freeze); a TTL shorter than the lag makes honest mirrors unusable.

seams.contract: The licence gate (astronomy L400 #21 rule: keep NC) runs before signing; licence and attribution_sha256 are inside the signed manifest; credit lines are verbatim.
seams.risk: A builder update relicenses Gaia-derived data as CC-BY-4.0, or a mirror strips the acknowledgement - both silently, unless the gate and the signature cover them.

Only appears because science floats (astronomy), byte-exact hashes (cryptography) and re-serialising replicas (distributed systems) meet.
failureLab.symptom: Scorecard FAIL 9/12: M4 rounds {1: null, 2: null, 3: null, 4: null} with conflicts on releases/v1..v3/catalogue.json; M5 rejects m2 ('v4: catalogue.json missing or changed'); S1 mirrors_agree false (JCS 6,536 bytes vs 7,901).

failureLab.fix: Canonical bytes everywhere: the producer, manifests, timestamps and log entries use RFC 8785 JCS; mirrors store bytes verbatim, and a re-encoding mirror must use JCS (idempotent: dumps(loads(x)) == x); clients parse with loads_strict. The number formatter is the build task.
failureLab.test: labs/L600/06-signed-science-data/tests/test_failure_lab.py (fault reproduces; fixed world converges) and labs/L600/06-signed-science-data/tests/test_build_task.py: BUILD_TARGET=mine on the shipped repr() formatter -> FAILED (failures=3); solution -> OK

buildTask.task: Implement number(x) in build_task/jcs_number.py so doubles are written as ECMAScript Number::toString (RFC 8785 3.2.2.3): shortest round-trip digits, no '.0' on integral values, plain decimals for 1e-6 <= |x| < 1e21, exponent form 'de+N'/'d.ddde-N' otherwise, -0 -> 0, NaN/Infinity/booleans refused.
hints: Python's repr() already gives the shortest digits; extract digits and the decimal exponent, then lay them out with the 4 ECMA-262 cases.
Test against RFC 8785 Appendix B, not against your own output.
buildTask.acceptance: BUILD_TARGET=mine python -m unittest tests.test_build_task -> Ran 5 tests, OK (shipped file: FAILED (failures=3)).

scalingLimits: Full-catalogue releases: Gaia DR3 has ~1.8 billion sources; one JSON file per release stops working long before that. Signal: release build time and mirror transfer grow linearly with every version. Move to chunked files (one leaf per chunk) so the Merkle manifest and anti-entropy work per chunk.

Gossip with 16 buckets: with millions of objects every differing bucket ships its full key list. Signal: anti-entropy bytes per round approach the delta size times bucket fan-out; deepen the bucket tree (Dynamo-style per key range).

Freshness at scale: thousands of clients behind slow mirrors hit expiry when lag approaches TTL. Signal: rising 'timestamp expired' refusals correlated with gossip rounds (tryIt 2). Re-sign more often or add a CDN-served timestamp; a single log also needs witnesses before clients can detect split views.

glossary.meaning: RFC 8785: one byte form for a JSON value - sorted keys (UTF-16 order), no whitespace, ECMAScript number layout.
Naming or checking data by its hash; any changed byte gives a different address.
RFC 9162: leaf = SHA-256(0x00||d), node = SHA-256(0x01||l||r); one root commits to an ordered list.
log2-sized hash paths proving an entry is in a tree, or that a newer tree extends an older one.
Background replica repair: compare summaries (Merkle roots), then exchange only differences.
Serving validly signed but older data / the same outdated data forever (TUF).
valid_through_version: a rotated key still counts for the releases it signed, never for new ones.
Two signatures (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) both required; secure if either scheme holds.

code:
"""L600 #06 - a verifiable, replicated science-data release pipeline (astronomy x cryptography x distributed systems).

python run_project.py                       -> scorecard as JSON lines; exit 0 only if every check passes
python run_project.py --inject float-format -> the failure lab: mirror m2 re-serialises JSON with '%.17g' doubles
other seeded faults: drop-old-key (rotation forgets old keys), no-freshness (client skips expiry/version checks),
licence-drop (builder uses astronomy L400 #21's unfixed licence function)

Flow: science.py (process) -> publisher.py (licence gate, files, Merkle manifest, Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 signatures,
transparency log, timestamp) -> mirrors.py (upload to m0, anti-entropy to m1-m3) -> client.py (verify everything).
world.py runs that story once; checks.py holds every milestone, seam and fitness check (tests call the same code).
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time

import checks
from world import World

FAULTS = ["float-format", "drop-old-key", "no-freshness", "licence-drop"]


def diagnose(w):
    """Failure-lab helper: show the first differing bytes of the catalogue between m0 and m2."""
    a = w.mirrors[0].objects.get("releases/v1/catalogue.json", b"")
    b = w.mirrors[2].objects.get("releases/v1/catalogue.json", b"")
    i = next((k for k in range(min(len(a), len(b))) if a[k] != b[k]), None)
    if i is None:
        return None
    start = a.rfind(b",", 0, i) + 1
    return {"m0": a[start:start + 34].decode(), "m2": b[start:start + 34].decode(), "offset": i}


def main(inject=None, only=None):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    w = World(inject)
    results = []
    for kind, cid, title, fn in checks.CHECKS:
        if only and cid not in only:
            continue
        ok, detail = fn(w)
        results.append(ok)
        print(json.dumps({"kind": kind, "id": cid, "title": title, "pass": ok, **detail}))
    if inject == "float-format":
        print(json.dumps({"kind": "diagnose", "first_difference_v1_catalogue": diagnose(w)}))
    print(json.dumps({"scorecard": "PASS" if all(results) else "FAIL", "passed": sum(results), "total": len(results),
                      "inject": inject, "seconds": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 1)}))
    return all(results)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--inject", choices=FAULTS, help="reproduce a seeded fault")
    ap.add_argument("--only", nargs="*", help="run only these check ids, e.g. --only S1 F2")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    sys.exit(0 if main(args.inject, args.only) else 1)

title: A reliable quantum-job service on unreliable backends
description: A job service that canonicalises OpenQASM circuits, caches results by canonical hash + backend + calibration version, schedules across three simulated noisy backends, survives retries, lease expiries, an outage and recalibrations, and returns exact shot totals with error bars.
outcome: You can find and guard the seams where quantum results, at-least-once execution and service architecture meet: exact shot accounting under duplicate execution, a cache key that respects circuit equivalence and calibration versions, and a result contract that always carries uncertainty.
environment: Mac mini or Windows 11; Python 3.12 venv; numpy 2.5.3; stdlib otherwise. Reuses labs from quantum-computing (L100 #5, L300 #12-13, L400 #17, _shared/qsim), distributed-systems (L200 #7) and application-architecture (L300 #13, #15, L400 #21) through _kb.py. Discrete-event simulation on a fake clock. SDK path (pending CI): a Qiskit Aer backend behind the same Backend interface - not built.
overview: Submit -> canonicalise -> versioned cache -> scheduler -> per-backend queues behind bulkheads and breakers -> leased, fenced chunk attempts -> result with error bars.
The interesting bugs are at the seams: a redelivered chunk inflates N, two texts of one circuit miss the cache, a recalibration stales cached results, a result without uncertainty misleads.

designBrief.context: Clients submit small OpenQASM circuits (2-4 qubits) with shots, a seed and a minimum estimated fidelity. Three backends differ: fast-noisy (4 slots, 1 s/chunk), slow-clean (2 slots, 3 s/chunk, 15% of chunks 5x slower) and flaky-mid (3 slots, 25% start rejections, a 40 s outage). Two backends recalibrate during the run. Clients retry submissions.

a cache hit never crosses a calibration version (0 crossings)

designBrief.question: How must chunk attempts, the cache key and the scheduler be designed so that duplicates, drift and outages never change what a client receives?

architecture.summary: jobservice.JobService is a discrete-event simulation on the quantum topic's FakeClock. submit() fingerprints the request (idempotency key), canonicalises the QASM (canon.py: L100 #5 reader, cancel adjacent self-inverse pairs, sorted ASAP moments) and looks up the result cache keyed on canonical hash + backend + calibration version + shots + seed. On a miss, pick() applies the fidelity floor, then a 15 s wait target, then the best estimated fidelity, and the job's 1000-shot chunks join that backend's queue. dispatch() honours the bulkhead (slots) and the backend's CircuitBreaker; each attempt gets a lease (10 s) and a fencing token. finish() executes the chunk on the L300 #12 noise model and commits it to the ledger: a FencedStorage slot per chunk, one calibration version per job (a newer version restarts the job). result() builds counts, probabilities with standard errors, and readout-mitigated values with propagated errors.
